title: Pipelined token fastpath with asymmetric NCCL concurrency
creator: Priya Malik
description:
Problem: Under mixed prefill/decode workloads we observe spiky latency and underutilized GPU compute where some ranks sit idle waiting for NCCL collectives or for large prefill bundles. Current strategies either: (a) aggressively serialize communication to make behavior deterministic and waste compute overlap, or (b) opportunistically overlap comm but starve small decode requests. Goal: Reduce p50/p95 latency for single-token decode paths while maintaining or improving total throughput for multi-token prefill batches across tensor+pipeline parallel topologies.

Proposal: Implement a 'pipelined token fastpath' that combines three ideas: (1) asymmetric NCCL concurrency windows — allow a small subset of ranks to enter limited concurrent collectives for short decode windows while others continue prefill work, (2) per-request micro-handshake between pipeline stages to enable early KV handoff without waiting for full batch boundary, (3) kernel pivot table for attention: select a low-latency fused attention kernel (flash/packed) for short sequences and the high-throughput tiled kernel for long prefill sequences.

Design details:
- Micro-handshake: introduce a lightweight control message (handshake token) passed between pipeline stage leaders. For incoming decode requests, stage leader can request a 'fastpath slot' from an admission controller on the local host (in-process token ring). If granted, that rank is permitted to start an NCCL subgroup allgather/allreduce limited to the minimal KV shards required for the decode window. Other ranks continue prefill.
- Asymmetric NCCL windows: use NCCL group calls in a constrained mode (subcommunicators or point-to-point friendly collectives) to allow overlap without breaking global consistency. Implement a configurable cap (e.g., max_concurrent_decode_ranks=2) and a short lease (e.g., 8ms) so decode windows are ephemeral. When a decode finishes or lease expires, collectives are drained and membership returns to the full prefill group.
- Kernel pivot table: extend kernel selection logic to consider both seq_len and active-concurrency flag. For seq_len <= 32 and when running in fastpath, choose flash-attention fused kernel optimized for single-step decode. For seq_len > 64 or when in prefill group, prefer tiled attention kernels that maximize throughput. This mapping is driven by offline microbenchmarks and runtime telemetry.
- KV prefilling handshake: allow partial KV shard materialization. During prefill, instead of waiting for full KV to be assembled across all shards, pipeline stages can publish 'KV-ready' bitmasks per-shard; decode fastpath can use available shards with local interpolation and request missing shards via prioritized subcollectives.

Implementation milestones:
- M1 (spike, 1wk): Prototype micro-handshake in emulator with local-threaded conductor and synthetic NCCL mock to validate correctness and fastpath admission semantics.
- M2 (integration, 2w): Implement asymmetric NCCL windowing using NCCL Communicators / NvPeerAccess where applicable; add admission controller and lease timers.
- M3 (kernel integration, 1w): Extend kernel selector with pivot table and tests; integrate with runtime sampling for seq_len distribution.
- M4 (end-to-end, 2w): Integrate KV-prefill bitmask protocol, validate on 8xA100 and 4xL40 topologies, run benchmark suite.
- M5 (rollout, 1w): Canary on dedicated pool, monitor p50/p95, fallback to conservative mode on regressions.

Metric targets / Acceptance criteria:
- p50 single-token decode latency reduction >= 25% vs baseline on mixed workload (50% prefill, 50% single-token random arrival).
- p95 decode latency no worse than baseline + 10% in steady-state.
- Aggregate throughput (tokens/sec) for batch prefills within 5% of baseline.
- NCCL tail times and GPU utilization improvements: reduce idle periods where >20% of ranks idle for >5ms.

Benchmarks and telemetry:
- Synthetic arrivals (Poisson) mixed with synthetic prefill sizes (8..1024). Measure per-stage GPU compute percentage, NCCL call durations, number of subgroup collectives, and kernel selection distribution.
- Real-app replay using traces from 3 customer workloads (ask analytics team for trace IDs). Capture token-level latencies, cost-per-token, and KV completeness rates.

Rollout and safety:
- Feature gated behind runtime flag: mgpu.fastpath.asymmetric_nccl=true. Default off for Dedicated until validated.
- Canary: enable on small subset of Dedicated pools (internal only) with real traffic, with automatic revert on SLO regressions (p95 decode > baseline+10% or throughput drop >8%).
- Logging: emit structured events for admission decisions, lease expirations, and fallback triggers for postmortem.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: NCCL subgrouping may interact poorly with certain network topologies (RoCE, IB) -> mitigation: add topology-aware disable and fall back to serialized mode.
- Risk: Partial KV usage can degrade output quality if shards missing -> mitigation: enforce correctness checks and degrade to full-collective mode for sensitive API keys/customers.
- Risk: Increased code complexity in kernel selection -> mitigation: keep pivot table declarative and add comprehensive unit microbenchmarks.

Open questions:
- Should admission controller be centralized per-host or fully distributed? Prototype favors in-process per-host ring for lower latency.
- How many concurrent decode ranks are optimal for typical 8x GPU racks? Start with 1-2 and experiment.
- What is the safe lease duration across GPU generations? Will require empirical tuning per topology.

2025-02-24 - Jasper Liu: Implemented admission token ring and lease timers. Observed a race where lease expiry overlaps with prefill completion; added drain barrier to avoid double-freeing communicator state.

2025-03-03 - SRE: Ran early benchmarks on 4xL40 cluster. p50 improved ~27% for single-token decode, but p95 regressed on some burst patterns. Need tuning of lease duration and max_concurrent_decode_ranks.
